prompt: Implement isEven and isOdd for n >= 0 using MUTUAL recursion: each method is defined by calling the other. Complete both stubs, then run the tests.
explanation: Mutual recursion is recursion spread across two methods: isEven delegates to isOdd and vice versa, and each hop shrinks n by 1 until a base case at 0 settles the question. The two base cases must disagree -- 0 is even and not odd -- or every answer would come out the same. The calls bounce back and forth n times, which is fine for the modest values in the tests but shows why direct checks like n % 2 are preferred in real code.
hints: Give each method its own base case at n == 0: isEven(0) is true, isOdd(0) is false.
For n > 0, isEven(n) should return isOdd(n - 1) -- it calls the OTHER method, not itself.
Symmetrically, isOdd(n) returns isEven(n - 1). Each call reduces n by 1 until one of the base cases is reached.
